title: NEXUSFlow: A Multi-Boat Autonomous Survey System for Locating Bank-Side Arsenic Sources in Rivers—System Design and Monte Carlo Evaluation
content: Arsenic contamination of the Kok River in northern Thailand is currently monitored by manual sampling at fixed points, and laboratory results take three to four weeks, while the source often remains unknown. We present NEXUSFlow, a monitoring system in which a fleet of five autonomous surface vehicles surveys a river reach along automatically planned zigzag routes, a plume-mapping model (PatternTrack AI) estimates the contaminant field and traces its source, and an AI agent (NATEE) drafts a response plan that is released only after approval by a pollution control officer and a village leader. To test the central design choice—mobile zigzag sampling instead of fixed stations—we ran a Monte Carlo simulation of 2,000 bank-side discharges in a 12 km reach using a two-dimensional transverse-mixing model with reflecting banks. The median full-mixing length was 46 km, so plumes remained attached to one bank throughout the reach. In the 1,776 scenarios in which some location exceeded 0.01 mg/L, seven fixed stations on one bank detected the plume in 38% of cases, stations on both banks in 75%, mid-channel stations in 2% and a centreline boat in 4%, whereas a 40-sample zigzag survey detected 83%. A short follow-up along the affected bank reduced the median source-location error to 15 m, compared with about 830 m for fixed stations. The ranking was unchanged for strongly meandering reaches. A prototype run on simulated data took 81 min from the first report to a village alert. The results support combining mobile zigzag surveys with fixed stations and must be confirmed by field tests.
